topic: Write a Story about a Misunderstanding in English(写一个英语误会的小故事)
genre: 记叙文 / 小故事(tell a story about a misunderstanding caused by English)
source: 外研社必修一 Unit 2 Developing ideas / Presenting ideas:write a story about a misunderstanding in English(根据情境写一段经历,讲清人物、地点、发生了什么、误会的原因)。
prompt_cn: 假设你叫李华,去年暑假你住在一个英国家庭。请用英语写一个约80词的小故事,内容包括:① 故事中的人物和地点;② 发生了什么(一个由英语词语引起的误会);③ 误会是怎么解开的、你的感受。可用 'I was really surprised when…', 'It turned out that…' 等表达。
prompt_en: Suppose you are Li Hua. Last summer you stayed with a British family. Write a short story (about 80 words) including: 1) who was in the story and where it happened; 2) what happened — a misunderstanding caused by an English word; 3) how the misunderstanding was cleared up and how you felt. You may use 'I was really surprised when…' and 'It turned out that…'.
points: 交代人物与地点(Last summer, I stayed with a British family.)
描述误会(I was really surprised when … / I wasn't sure whether …)
解开误会(It turned out that …)
表达感受、句句围绕这个误会
model_essay: Last summer, I stayed with a British family. One evening, the mother said we would have 'toad-in-the-hole' for dinner. I was really surprised, because I thought a toad was an animal like a frog. I wasn't sure whether I should eat it, so I said nothing. It turned out that the dish was just sausages baked in a kind of cake, and it was delicious! Everyone laughed when I explained my mistake. That funny misadventure taught me never to judge an English dish by its strange name.
model_translation: 去年夏天,我住在一个英国家庭。一天傍晚,女主人说晚饭吃'洞中蟾蜍'。我大吃一惊,因为我以为蟾蜍是像青蛙一样的动物。我不确定该不该吃,就什么也没说。结果那道菜其实是裹在面糊里烤的香肠,非常美味!我解释我的误会时,大家都笑了。那次有趣的倒霉经历让我明白,不能凭奇怪的名字来判断一道英国菜。

rubric.criteria: 三要素齐全:人物地点 / 误会经过 / 解开与感受
按时间顺序讲故事、句句围绕这个误会、代词指代清楚、行文连贯
记叙时态正确、词汇句型准确多样、构词/搭配运用得当、语法基本无误

required_structure: 开头 Last summer, I stayed with a British family.
误会 I was really surprised when … / I wasn't sure whether …
转折 It turned out that …
结尾 That funny misadventure taught me …
key_expressions: I was really surprised when she said we would have 'toad-in-the-hole'.
I wasn't sure whether I should eat it.
It turned out that the dish was just sausages baked in a kind of cake.
That funny misadventure taught me never to judge a dish by its name.

high_sentences: I was really surprised when the mother said we would have 'toad-in-the-hole'.
I wasn't sure whether I should eat it, so I said nothing.
It turned out that the dish was just sausages baked in a kind of cake.
That funny misadventure taught me never to judge an English dish by its strange name.

error_pairs.wrong: I was surprised when she say that.
error_pairs.correct: I was surprised when she said that.
error_pairs.note: 记叙过去的事,从句动词用过去式 said。

error_pairs.wrong: It turned out that the dish is sausages.
error_pairs.correct: It turned out that the dish was sausages.
error_pairs.note: 主句过去时,宾语从句也用过去时保持一致。

error_pairs.wrong: I wasn't sure whether eat it or not.
error_pairs.correct: I wasn't sure whether to eat it or not.
error_pairs.note: whether 后接动词不定式用 whether to do。

第5句 感受:That funny misadventure taught me …
